liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (1 review): The crowd noticeably swells when Jerry starts singing this song [19]
- **Ripple** (1 review): Taper had to flip the tape near the end of Ripple, causing a brief gap [13]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Taper seems to have been dancing during this song, audible on the recording [14]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer finds this one only so-so, following a nice jam after drums [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **amazing how the Phillies won**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-23.aud.morris.108016.flac24** (recommended): audience recording; 31 songs; 206 min [1]
- **gd1980-10-23.120072.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: source not stated; 28 songs; 197 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd80-10-23.cohen.vernon.13140.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 28 songs; 182 min; rated 4.47/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording conveys the room's energy well, especially on headphones; Clear, centered, hiss-free audience recording; Complete show with unusually good sound for a 1980 audience recording [10][13][17]
- **gd80-10-23.sonyecm280.wiley.8700.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 27 songs; 190 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Sony ECM280 audience tape has too much crowd noise, though no better source was known [18]
- **gd1980-10-23.143352.fob.nak700.cohen.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 28 songs; 184 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer pictures the Radio City crowd moving, dancing and singing, with audible heckles to sit down and smells of the hall [10]
- Seat was under the mezzanine edge, somewhat left of center, about the 29th row [15]
- Attendee decided at around 4pm to go, driving from New Haven after a friend's brother arrived with tickets [16]
- During the first set someone nearby repeatedly yells for people to sit down, which is audible on the tape [21]
- Early in the run, so the acoustic set stood out; the 10/25 and 10/26 shows are also good [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-23.aud.morris.108016.flac24**: taped by Bob Morris; transferred by Bob Morris; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM-300 (CP-1) x2 > Cassette Master (Marantz Superscope CD320/TDK SA-C90 except Set 3: Maxell UDXLII-C90) [1]. Also: Patched with the Sony ECM280 source in parts of the acoustic set, including Roses; Drums tape flip spliced and dropouts edited [1]
- **gd1980-10-23.120072.fob-nak700.gatto-jaeger.dusborne.flac16**: taped by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; transferred by Michael Turi; source: Loge Dead front center; Nak 700 > sony D-5> AMC> DAT> CDR> EAC> TLH> Flac; Recorded by Keith Gatto & Pete Jaeger; Extracted & flac encoded by Michael Turi;… [2]
- **gd80-10-23.cohen.vernon.13140.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Mark Cohen; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [3]. Also: Recorded by Marc Cohen with Nakamichi microphones and a Sony D5 deck; Taped from orchestra Row C, seat 224, with Nakamichi CM-700 mics into a Sony TC-D5M using Dolby B; Cassette was digitized via Tascam 122MKIII, DA-40 DAT and CD burner; taper recorded four or five Radio City nights [14][15]
- **gd80-10-23.sonyecm280.wiley.8700.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280 mics [4]
- **gd1980-10-23.143352.fob.nak700.cohen.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Cohen; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Cohen's (FOB) Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5 (located in the orchestra seats) [5]. Also: From Mark Cohen's master cassette, freshly transferred by Charlie Miller; notes mention channel dropouts, skips and cuts in earlier versions [5]
